claims.text: A thin, coherent Ni interlayer can act as a transition medium between diffusion-mediated and dislocation-mediated creep in HEA multilayers.
HEA multilayers with highly coherent interfaces primarily exhibit diffusion-mediated creep at lower-stress and lower-temperature conditions.
Incorporating a thin Ni interlayer at the interfaces will modulate interface coherency.
Ni has a moderate self-diffusivity relevant to the proposed creep transition.
The crystal structure of Ni contributes to its ability to mediate the proposed creep transition.
A Ni interlayer can retain sufficient interface coherency for vacancy-mediated creep at lower stresses.
At increased stress or temperature, the Ni interlayer facilitates dislocation nucleation.
At increased stress or temperature, the Ni interlayer facilitates dislocation glide.

The combination of vacancy-mediated creep at lower stress and enhanced dislocation activity at higher stress or temperature will enable a transition between diffusion-dominated and dislocation-dominated creep.
Compared with HEA multilayers without Ni interlayers, the modified multilayers will have a reduced diffusion-creep rate at lower stress or temperature.
Compared with HEA multilayers without Ni interlayers, the modified multilayers will show a greater contribution from dislocation creep at higher stress or temperature.
The proposed creep-mechanism transition will produce changes in the creep exponent.
The proposed creep-mechanism transition will produce observable changes in microstructural dislocation features.
The transition effect will be significant only within an optimal range of Ni interlayer thickness.
The transition effect will be significant only at temperatures and stresses near the creep-mechanism transition regime.
Outside the optimal thickness and transition-regime conditions, the Ni-modified interface may not effectively bridge diffusion-mediated and dislocation-mediated creep.
